dedupe_keys.name: qgas interactive map based toolkit for building and editing topology consistent gas hydrogen and co2 infrastructure datasets

description: QGas, from the energy economics institute at Graz University of Technology, is an interactive toolkit for visualising, creating and collaboratively extending georeferenced gas infrastructure datasets, described in an April 2026 arXiv paper by Quantschnig, Werner, Wogrin and Klatzer. It combines GIS geometry editing with topology-preserving graph operations in a web-based map built with Python, JavaScript and Leaflet. Users can draw and reroute pipelines, add hydrogen pipelines, storage, LNG terminals and other assets, repurpose existing pipes, manage attributes, and georeference scanned infrastructure plans as background images to digitise networks. A topology checker reports reference, connectivity, geometry, duplicate identifier, crossing and disconnected network issues, per-session logs and undo keep edits traceable, and complete, filtered or changed data can be exported as GeoJSON or CSV. The paper extends a natural gas dataset with hydrogen and CO2 infrastructure as an example. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): MIT. Access is free of charge. Coverage is any user dataset. Simulation uses are preparing consistent multi-carrier gas network topologies for energy system and network flow models. Related records: model-gasnetsim simulates flows on such networks. The underlying files were not downloaded, so their contents are not verified here.
